solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: More than one criminal child is involved in creative pursuits (9)

indicators.note: SON and IS are caught up inside ARTS

explanation.surface: A worried note about a gifted but delinquent youngster who has taken up painting and music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double duty in the surface as a verb, but in the wordplay it is just two letters that go into ARTS alongside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsonists are criminals, and the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Passage under a home? No (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, WAY sits below A

blocks.note: a road or route you pass along

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tunnel runs beneath a house, and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is split across a question and its reply: not 'home' is AWAY, as in a football fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a question answered no: an away match is played anywhere but your own ground.

clue.text: Society in need engaging partners at table who will provide cash (7)

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the person who provides cash

indicators.note: POOR takes on NS, holding it inside

blocks.note: North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A charity dinner where needy guests hope the people at their table will pay.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge the four players are named by compass points, and North and South play as partners, so 'partners' gives NS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is someone who puts up money for a person or event.

clue.text: No errant suitor embraces love like Don Juan? (9)

indicators.note: straying from its course, so SUITOR's letters wander
the rearranged SUITOR holds O inside it

explanation.surface: A wandering suitor who loves anyone going, just like the legendary seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Don Juan is the byword for a notorious womaniser, and 'suitor' and 'love' keep the surface on him.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is famous for his bad reputation, which is what notorious means.

clue.text: Plain stage, place emptied out (6)

indicators.note: PLACE loses its contents, leaving only P and E

blocks.note: a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A bare theatre set, the venue cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective describing the stage, but it is a noun: a flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless plain, as in Central Asia.

clue.text: Holy soldiers lament having interred one saint somewhere inside church (8)

indicators.note: CRY buries I and ST inside it

blocks.note: the Salvation Army, a Christian body organised like an army

explanation.surface: Crusaders mourning as they bury a saint somewhere within a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy soldiers' suggests crusaders, but it is the Salvation Army, SA.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacristy is the room in a church where vestments and sacred vessels are kept.

clue.text: Down-and-out old boy entering house (4)

indicators.note: to enter is to go into, so the old boy goes into the house

explanation.surface: A destitute former pupil finds shelter in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a school, abbreviated OB.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an American word for a tramp who drifts from place to place with no settled home.

clue.text: I’m confused having accepted politician’s expression of discontent (5)

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so HUH takes the politician in

blocks.note: huh? is what you say when puzzled

explanation.surface: A bewildered voter grumbles after taking in a politician's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm confused' has to be heard as something said, HUH, rather than a statement about the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Humph is a grunt of doubt or displeasure.

clue.text: Item of food — it goes into bottomless hole (7)

indicators.note: IT is placed inside BURRO
in a down clue the last letter is the bottom, so BURROW loses W

blocks.note: a burrow is a hole; without its last letter W

explanation.surface: A snack disappears down a pit with no floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottomless' suits a down clue: the bottom of BURROW is its final W.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican tortilla wrap.

clue.text: Head of academic staff welcomes street preacher (7)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of academic
to welcome a guest is to take them in, so the staff takes in the street

explanation.surface: A university department head greets a street evangelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of academic staff' reads as one job title; split it, and 'staff' is a stick, POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles went out preaching the gospel.

clue.text: Cold Italian region identical to English one (7)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as on a tap
Umbria is a region of central Italy

explanation.surface: A chilly Italian region is said to be the twin of an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' in the definition points back to 'region': Cumbria is the county of the Lake District in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is a region, a county, of England.

clue.text: Elaborate embellishment involving funny tiger and tea (8)

indicators.note: strange, out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fancy decoration featuring a comic tiger at a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' looks like an anagram indicator, but it belongs to the definition; the instruction is 'funny'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is an ornamental plume or jewelled spray worn on a hat or in the hair.

clue.text: One faced with predicament in row? This could offer some illumination (5,8)

indicators.note: I is placed in front of PLIGHT
I PLIGHT goes inside STRING

blocks.note: a string is a row, as of beads or wins

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a quarrel hopes for a bit of enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, which suits 'predicament', but it is a line of things, STRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Strip lighting is long fluorescent tubes, which light a room.

clue.text: All-encompassing means of stopping undesirable elements? (8)

blocks.note: covering a whole range of things beneath it, as a term or organisation can
the elements are the weather; this keeps rain off

explanation.surface: A catch-all way of keeping out unwanted people.
explanation.walkthrough: The elements here are the weather, not bad people in society: an umbrella term covers everything, and an umbrella keeps rain off.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella organisation or term covers everything under it; an umbrella keeps off rain.

clue.text: Vegetable foodstuff essential to bones? (6)

blocks.note: a large green squash, the overgrown cousin of the courgette
the soft tissue at the core of a bone

explanation.surface: A vegetable said to be vital for healthy bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' carries its sense of 'at the essence': marrow is what lies at the core of a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrow is both a squash and the tissue inside bones.

clue.text: Manage after form of therapy to get hold of huge medical instrument (8)

indicators.note: placed after, so the word for manage follows the therapy
to get hold of something is to grip it, so the therapy-plus-manage pair grips the size inside

explanation.surface: A patient copes after therapy by grabbing a giant piece of hospital kit.
explanation.walkthrough: OS for outsize is a clothing-size label.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the instrument a doctor uses to look inside the ear.

clue.text: Concept of modern physics raised issues involving velocity (5-4)

indicators.note: in a down clue EMITS is read bottom to top
the turned word takes PACE inside

explanation.surface: A physics idea that brought up questions about speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issues' is a verb, not a noun for problems as 'raised issues' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-time is the four-dimensional continuum of relativity.

clue.text: A divine Italian home including old extension (8)

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so the home word holds the old one

blocks.note: Doctor of Divinity; a divine is a clergyman
Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A heavenly Italian house with a period annexe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a noun, a theologian, hence DD; and 'Italian' is IT, the vermouth in gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the building sense: a new room built on to a house extends it.

clue.text: There may be a cafe here, by the way (8)

definitions.text: There may be a cafe here, by the way

blocks.clueFragment: There may be a cafe here
blocks.note: the surface reading: somewhere to stop for a cup of tea
reads as 'incidentally', but means literally beside the road

explanation.surface: A casual aside mentioning that there is somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' reads as a throwaway 'incidentally', but it means beside the way: a ROADSIDE cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside is the land beside a road, where cafes stand.

clue.text: Dispenser of perfume? Loos are transformed (7)

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: An air freshener transforms the lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' serves twice, as fodder and as the verb of the indicator phrase. The question mark admits that an aerosol can dispense many things besides perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, as the question mark admits: perfume is one of many things sold in a pressurised spray can.

clue.text: Phone back about computer program and flap (6)

indicators.note: TEL is turned round to LET
about means around, so the turned phone goes around the program

explanation.surface: An order to return a call about some software, and a bit of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flap' looks like a state of fluster; it is a hanging fold of cloth or skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lappet is a small flap or fold, as on a garment or headdress.

clue.text: Doughy grub? Dad eats nothing when fasting is fashionable (7)

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so PA takes the nothing and the fast in

blocks.note: the season when giving things up is in vogue

explanation.surface: A father tucks into nothing but stodge while dieting is in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when fasting is fashionable' is a playful definition of LENT, the forty days before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is a thick maize porridge, doughy food.

clue.text: Seafood bringing some regrets, you being upset (6)

indicators.note: only part of the words is used
in a down clue, the letters are turned upside down

blocks.note: the run of letters inside regRETS YOu, which the reversal turns round

explanation.surface: A plate of shellfish that leaves you ill and sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suggests a stomach after bad seafood; in a down clue it turns the letters over.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the oyster is one kind of shellfish served as seafood.

clue.text: Member of cabinet revised payroll, somehow dismissing aide finally (4,5,4)

indicators.note: in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged
one E is removed from the fodder

blocks.note: the last letter of aidE, which is dismissed

explanation.surface: A minister has rejigged the staff wages and quietly sacked an assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' looks like the anagram indicator, but it is fodder, and one of its E's is the aide's last letter to go. The Lord Privy Seal is a traditional senior post in the British cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Privy Seal is a UK government minister, usually in the cabinet.

clue.text: Face tackling a good heathen (5)

indicators.note: to tackle is to take hold of, so PAN takes hold of the letters

blocks.note: pan is slang for face, as in deadpan
A as it stands, then G for good, placed after the P

explanation.surface: Confronting a decent unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a verb to go with 'tackling'; it is a noun, PAN, as in deadpan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, someone outside the main religions.

clue.text: Feature of crossword — hard work with any number to be got out (4)

indicators.note: to get something out is to remove it, so N comes out of GRIND

blocks.note: n stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: Solving a crossword is a slog, with numbers to be worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the algebraic 'any number', as in the nth degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for part of the puzzle itself: the grid is the pattern of black and white squares the answers fill.

clue.text: Like leader of Samurai, say, with first-class sharp weapon (7)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Samurai

blocks.note: A1, first-class, with the 1 as I

explanation.surface: A Samurai chief carries a superb blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The Samurai surface points to a sword, but the weapon is African; A1 is written AI, with the numeral read as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender Southern African spear.

clue.text: Problem with concentration? Maybe this is needed for the solution (7)

definitions.text: Maybe this is needed for the solution

blocks.note: a mixture that is too dilute has a concentration problem

blocks.clueFragment: Maybe this is needed for the solution
blocks.note: a solvent that dilutes paint into a solution

explanation.surface: A solver who can't focus reckons a break is needed to crack the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves pretend to be about a solver's mind; the concentration and the solution are chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Too weak a concentration is thinner; thinner is the liquid that dilutes paint.

clue.text: Food enthusiast needing large input (4)

indicators.note: FAN requires something added
input is something put in, so L goes into FAN

explanation.surface: A keen eater who needs a big helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food enthusiast' reads as a foodie, but the definition stops at 'Food'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: flan, an open pastry tart, is one kind of food.

clue.text: Rude man is wrong person to be looking after children (9)

definitions.text: person to be looking after children

indicators.note: the letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An ill-mannered man is unsuited to childcare.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says who should not look after children, and the anagram gives the person who should.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children.
